reasoning: The extract has no citations (empty references and links), so everything rests on the stated plans. It contains no real success measures, but it does set out some evaluation plans. Lines such as "We will carry out a further review before legislating... to enable consideration of the latest life expectancy projections and to allow us to evaluate the effects of current rises in State Pension age" explain why a review is needed. The line "The legislation provides for the next State Pension age review to be conducted by July 2023" gives a timetable. "In the interim period the Government will analyse the impact of changes to State Pension age already in train – i.e. the equalisation... and the rise from age 65 to 66" says what will be evaluated. "The Government intends to continue to monitor the effects of State Pension age rises alongside the reforms to the state and private pension systems, the welfare system, and the labour market" points to ongoing monitoring. "These will be produced for an impact assessment accompanying legislation at the appropriate time" gives a vague output and timing. This reaches Level 2: there is a plan for evaluation with a review date and a rationale. The strongest counter-example to a higher level is the absence of specific outcome measures, such as employment rates, health or poverty indicators. The extract also says nothing about testing the policy first, consultation, or publication of results. The impact assessment is only said to accompany legislation, with no commitment to publish the evaluation findings. To reach Level 3, the document would need to name the outcomes to be measured, explain how the evaluation will be done, and commit to publishing the results with a timetable.
